To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) in a market in which informed traders can place either market orders or demand schedules, market orders are more common than demand schedules, and the market is less informative when market orders are common; (ii) the market can be fully informative even when market orders dominate the market; and (iii) when demand schedules are more costly than market orders, market orders dominate the trading when the precision of the signals goes to infinity.

the composition of the trading market by order type is endogenous, and that the market is more price-informative when the order type that is more informative of the asset's dividend is used more frequently.

(i) in a large market, the composition of order types is endogenous, (ii) the composition is such that price informativeness is always bounded, and (iii) the composition is independent of the precision of information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between the composition of a market by order type and its efficiency.
the interplay between the composition of a market by order types and the informativeness of its price.
the interplay between the composition of the order book, the quality of information and the price informativeness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the market is more price-informative the lower the cost of demand schedules, and that it is more price-informativeness the higher the cost of demand schedule, but only up to a point.
, as the precision of information goes to infinity and the cost of demand schedules to zero, market-order traders overwhelm and the price becomes uninformatively noisy.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, when the market is dominated by market orders, the price becomes more informative as the precision of private information increases.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the composition of the trading market by order type may be a key determinant of price informativeness, even when the order types are endogenous.
the market composition by order type is an endogenous outcome that depends on market microstructure, the distribution of traders' private signals and the precision of the latter.
, when the precision of information about the asset goes to infinity, the market is dominated by market orders and the price is not informative.
